0: Here we get straight to Claude Code: from installation and sign-in, to connecting a model, and on to using it in your own project.
1: If you want AI to help you change code, organise writing, or build a small tool you use every day, follow along.
3: Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding tool. Give it a task and it can read project files, analyse the implementation, change code and run commands to check the result.
4: Its working process can be understood as: understand the requirement → look at the files → make a plan → carry out the changes → check the result.
5: For example, you can ask it to explain a project you cannot follow, track down an error, add a feature, or read local Markdown articles to generate summaries, tidy a table of contents or rewrite them for different platforms.
6: This article mainly uses the terminal version. After installing, type claude in the project folder to start a conversation; if you prefer a graphical interface you can also choose the desktop app or editor integrations. Claude Code overview
7: Get one small task working first, then add project rules, Skills and external tools step by step.
8: Screenshots illustrate where to click and what the interface looks like; the exact version, model names and plan details are those shown on the actual page. Use the code blocks in the text for commands.
